obligations.note: The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen maps to manage_payees, which is in rbac.PRIVILEGED, but routes.py sets mfa=False. The exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails on head 30fdc36, flagging exactly this route, and no valid exception covers it.

EXC-0258 is approved by risk owner Omar Haddad, not the requester, and unexpired (2026-11-23), but it is scoped to component payments.http. The deviation (mfa=False) lives in routes.py, component payments.routes, and it disables MFA for every manage_payees caller, not just the reconciliation batch account, so the exception is out of scope.
The change's CI run on the final commit 30fdc36 has result 'failure': 1 of 172 tests failed, the registered MFA-1 control test. No tests were added for the new route despite the PR description.

Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1, exhaustive control test at e5bf646) covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/routes.py, which this change alters in behaviour. The only new evidence of the same strength is the failing control test, so MFA-1 has no valid evidence.

The new reopen_payee in service.py calls _audit, which records actor, action, target and clock time. However, the registered AUD-1 control test is only 'sample' coverage and does not exercise reopen, so the evidence is not exhaustive.

store.py gains reopen_payee, which updates only status and closed_at and touches no NPI column. The exhaustive control test test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed on head in the recorded CI run.
The new execute call in store.py uses a fixed SQL string literal with payee_id bound as a parameter. The exhaustive control test test_sql_statements_are_parameterized passed on head.

Ticket CHG-26710 was approved by change manager erik.brandt at 2026-10-27T07:37Z, before both reviews. Its components (payments.http, routes, service, store) cover every touched file per controls/payments/components.json.
The code_review approval comes from mara.costa, a payments change_approver and a different person from the author sofia.santos (p-ssantos).
Both approvals name the head commit 30fdc36, the only commit in the change.
The change touches security-sensitive components (routes, http, store). A security_review approval from ines.halvorsen (security_reviewer) names head 30fdc36.
The diff touches only apps/baseline-payments/payments/{app,routes,service,store}.py. No protected path (controls/, control tests, ci/) is changed, so no control_owner approval is needed.
The change is non-emergency (emergency=false, ticket type 'standard'), so no post-implementation review is due.

summary: The change adds POST /payees/{id}/reopen with mfa=False even though its action, manage_payees, is privileged, which violates MFA-1. The cited exception EXC-0258 is scoped to payments.http and the batch account, but MFA is disabled in routes.py (payments.routes) for all callers, so it does not cover the deviation. The change's own CI run on the final commit failed on the MFA-1 control test, and the earlier MFA-1 ledger evidence has lapsed because routes.py changed. The ticket, independent code review and security review are in order, but the product and testing violations require rejection.
